feedback: What I had to do in the controller: I kept the iteration 0 gains (kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5) rather than the iteration 1 gains (kp 0.6, kd 0.10), because iteration 1 changed the gains alongside the geometry and so could not be used to tune this isolated test. The iteration 0 race showed that the controller produced steering oscillation of 0.11 to 0.16 on all tracks and control_effort of 1.45 on the s-bend, so the geometry must be tested with the same gains to see whether the sensing lag or the gain is the limit. Iteration 1 showed that the lighter robot (0.6 kg, 0.10 m track) cut oval steering oscillation from 0.115 to 0.074 but also cut oval progress from 0.20 to 0.11, so I cannot yet say whether mass or track drives either result. Decision rules for the next race: if max_error falls below 0.06 m on the s-bend and oval, keep y = 0.04 m and move on to sensor pitch as the next isolated test. If max_error stays between 0.062 and 0.066 m but progress rises, the lag hypothesis is only partly right, so the next step is to raise kd in steps of about 0.03 with this sensor row, because a closer row will have less lead to damp overshoot. If progress falls below 0.16 with max_error unchanged, sensing is not the limit and the robot is too slow, so the next step is wheel_radius, not steering.
requested_changes: If max_error stays above 0.06 m on the s-bend and oval with y = 0.04 m, try wheel_track 0.14 m with all else unchanged, because iteration 0 control_effort on the s-bend was 1.45 and slalom was 1.36, which suggests the robot needs more turn authority than a 0.12 m track gives.

If the race finishes with progress at or above 0.16 but max_error still exceeds 0.06 m, try sensor_size 0.008 m at the same y = 0.04 m, because iteration 1 (16 mm sensors) did not clearly help and a smaller footprint may sharpen the centre-of-line signal on tight bends (a hypothesis from iteration 1 data, not a measured result).

If progress falls below the iteration 0 level of about 0.16 while max_error is unchanged, try wheel_radius 0.035 m, because iteration 0 progress of 0.12 to 0.20 is too low to finish within 3 s and a larger wheel gives more ground speed at the same PWM.
